Fit Blocks in a Container with a Minimum Number of Columns

April 2026
Expand for Details
  • This code makes divs that fill a container element (it's the prototype for the multi-player).
  • The number of rows and columns is determined automatically based on the width and height of the containing element.
  • A minimum of five columns are output.
  • A maximum width is defined for the div cells. More columns are added if two can be added without increasing beyond the max.
  • Columns are added in pairs so there's always an even number.
  • A width/height ratio is used to determine how tall the individual div cells are.

  • This is the key function that does the calculations: 

    function getLayout(d) {
  let cellWidth = Math.floor(d.containerWidth / d.minColumns);
  for (let columns = d.minColumns + 2; columns <= d.maxColumns; columns += 2) {
    const checkWidth = Math.floor(d.containerWidth / columns);
    if (checkWidth > d.maxWidth) {
      cellWidth = checkWidth;
    } else {
      break;
    }
  }
  const cellHeight = cellWidth / d.ratioWidth * d.ratioHeight;
  const columns = parseInt(d.containerWidth / cellWidth, 10);
  const rows = parseInt(d.containerHeight / cellHeight, 10);
  const cells = columns * rows;
  return {
    cellWidth: cellWidth,
    cellHeight: cellHeight,
    columns: columns,
    rows: rows,
    cells: cells,
  };
}

    I'm using it with bitty but that's not a requirement.

  • The bitty code looks like this:

    export const b = { init: "cells" };

export function cells(_, __, el) {
  const layout = getLayout(
    {
      maxWidth: el.propAsInt("maxWidth"),
      containerWidth: parseInt(el.getBoundingClientRect().width),
      containerHeight: parseInt(el.getBoundingClientRect().height),
      ratioWidth: el.propAsInt("ratioWidth"),
      ratioHeight: el.propAsInt("ratioHeight"),
      minColumns: 5,
      maxColumns: 19,
    },
  );
  el.replaceChildren();
  for (let i = 0; i < layout.cells; i = i + 1) {
    el.append(b.render("cell"));
  }
  b.setCSS("--cell-width", `${layout.cellWidth}px`);
  b.setCSS("--cell-height", `${layout.cellHeight}px`);
}

    which works with this div on the page:

    <div class="cells" data-r="cells" data-max-width="144" data-ratio-width="16" data-ratio-height="9">
  Loading Cells
</div>

    and this template:

    <script type="text/html" id="cellTemplate">
  <div class="cell">
    <img src="&#x2f;javascript&#x2f;fit-minimum-blocks-in-container/example-image.jpg" />
  </div>
</script>

  • The approach I'm using in the bitty script requires the container element have a pre-existing width and height. I'm doing that using this in the stylesheet: 

    * {
  margin: 0;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

html {
  scrollbar-gutter: stable;
}

body {
  background-color: var(--background-color);
  color: var(--default-color);
  min-height: 100svh;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto auto;
}

main {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
}

.cells {
  flex: 1;
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-content: flex-start;
  justify-content: center;
}

.cell {
  display: flex;
  width: var(--cell-width);
  height: var(--cell-height);
}

  • The overall structure of the page looks like this:

    <header></header>
<div class="prelude"></div>
<main></main>
<footer></footer>
<div class="support"></div>

    This section of the CSS sets up the `<main>` tag to take up all the space between the two leading elements (header and the prelude div) and the final two (footer and the support div):

    body {
  min-height: 100svh;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr auto auto;
}

    That's a cool technique I just learned from a Kevin Powell video. The rest of the CSS uses flex box to line everything up.
